news.title: Silver price: Correction brings key $50 level into focusOctober 25, 2026 As of October 23, 2026, by Florian Grummes In an environment marked by high uncertainty and tension, precious metals prices came under further pressure over the past two weeks. After trading sideways for around three weeks, gold broke below support at USD 4,065 yesterday and was sold off to USD 3,986 by the start of Asian trading this morning. The bears have left no doubt since late August about who is in control of the silver market. While the previous week had already produced a low of USD 55.40, the sell-off continued this week without any meaningful resistance . In early Asian trading today, the price fell to USD 53.45, clearly below the summer low of USD 54.40. Silver is now at its lowest price in eleven months . Given the correction underway since late January from USD 121.67 (-56%), sentiment is at rock bottom, and silver is once again being written off as “dead money.” Gold and silver price performance in 2026, as of October 23, 2026. © GOLD.DE Sovereign risk and the eurozone’s new fragility At the same time, France’s risk premium over Germany in the bond markets is approaching levels seen during the eurozone debt crisis: At around 175 basis points over German Bunds, the spread on 10-year French government bonds has reached a level that has historically often signaled broader market turmoil in the eurozone. The French 10-year yield recently climbed above five percent—a price signal with implications extending far beyond France. This is because the spread measures not only France’s creditworthiness, but also the fiscal and political cohesion of the monetary union. High debt, large deficits, political paralysis and social tensions ahead of the 2027 presidential election weigh on confidence, refinancing costs and risk appetite across the eurozone at the same time. Any investor with European exposure through equities, credit or the euro should therefore monitor this metric closely. France as the eurozone’s new stress test Moreover, France is not a peripheral outlier, but the eurozone’s second-largest economy. Rising French borrowing costs could also quickly spread to Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal through bank balance sheets, insurance portfolios and generally higher risk aversion. While the eurozone has strengthened its institutional framework since 2011, institutions are no substitute for credible fiscal policy. The ECB between firefighter and trap Spread between German and French 10-year government bonds, as of October 22, 2026. © GOLD.DE The ECB’s “Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI)” generally allows bond purchases when a country’s financing conditions tighten in an “unwarranted and disorderly” manner. However, France currently fails to meet precisely this requirement: A significant portion of the spread widening is the result of understandable fiscal and political risks and therefore cannot readily be classified as “unwarranted.” An Allianz research paper sums it up: Only in the event of broader fragmentation in the euro bond market —for example, with French spreads at around 175 basis points, Italian spreads at about 150 basis points, and spreads in Spain and Portugal rising at the same time— would the ECB likely take operational action . The TPI would probably only be considered if the French spread rises above 200 basis points and the Italian spread above 175 basis points Until then, the ECB could initially remain on the sidelines. The market penalty thus acts like an unintended but tangible tightening of monetary policy: More tax revenue goes toward debt service, while fewer funds are available for investment, education and social benefits . At the same time, borrowing becomes more expensive for businesses and households—with adverse consequences for growth, investment activity and purchasing power. Stock markets ignore mounting stress While the eurozone’s fundamentals are increasingly deteriorating and precious metals prices are correcting, equity markets continue to price in relative calm—even though stress is clearly building in the background. Markets are currently telling two contradictory stories. We discussed a similar picture last week for the S&P 500, where bullish and bearish market signals are appearing at the same time. These macroeconomic discrepancies are particularly noteworthy because, over the medium term, one of the two sides is highly likely to be wrong. The key question, therefore, is which market is telling the more fundamentally sound story—and which is merely being driven by momentum, positioning, and short-term capital flows. The silver price provides a textbook example of exactly this: Over the past nine months, the silver market has undergone a sharp and uncompromising correction—without signaling the end of the secular bull market. While the still-ongoing pullback toward USD 50 is an extremely unpleasant stress test for late entrants and a painful lesson in market volatility, anyone who has been active in the precious metals sector long enough knows that these are buying opportunities , as the structural drivers of the bull market remain intact. Correction does not mark the end of the cycle Silver combines monetary demand, industrial use and an extremely small market capitalization. This combination produces both strong upward moves and sharp pullbacks. Meanwhile, the debt crisis, uncertainty over real interest rates and geopolitical fragmentation remain unresolved, while industrial demand for silver, the “critical metal of the future,” is more likely to rise than fall going forward. If the French crisis were to broaden into wider euro fragmentation, the environment for precious metals would change fundamentally. Higher risk premiums, potential ECB intervention, fiscal dominance, and a weaker euro have historically provided favorable conditions for gold and silver . The current correction would then not contradict the crisis, but rather represent its effects being priced in ahead of time. Silver in US dollars – Extremely strong support around USD 50 Silver in US dollars, daily chart as of October 23, 2026. © GOLD.DE With an intraday low of 53.45 so far, silver today fell below its summer low of USD 54.77. Since August 28, the silver price has also essentially moved in only one direction—downward—as interim recoveries have been scarce since the summer high of USD 71.17. However, following a decline of around 25 percent within eight weeks, technical conditions are deeply oversold. The pullback toward USD 50 was to be expected within the decade-long cup-and-handle pattern and is not yet complete . The USD 50 level is crucial, as this is where the 1980 and 2011 highs were located. In the fall of 2025, silver broke above this threshold on a sustained basis for the first time—triggering the subsequent steep rise to USD 121.67. However, the correction underway since January does not automatically invalidate this breakout. So far, it appears to be testing the breakout level in classic fashion. For now, this leaves the daily and weekly charts bearish. Around USD 50, however, the bears are encountering increasingly strong support as well as contrarian buyers. The seasonal pattern also suggests that the final trend reversal should take place by around mid-December—and thus by the Fed’s final interest rate decision of the year. We are therefore not overly concerned. Instead, we now see good buying opportunities again at last in both precious metals and mining stocks, and are therefore consistently using the current period of weakness to make further purchases. Conclusion: Silver – Near its key level The sharp widening of France’s bond spread is once again exposing the fragile political and fiscal foundations of the eurozone. Silver, by contrast, is undergoing a painful but still constructive consolidation following an extreme period of overheating. Those who look only at the daily charts see two weak markets; those who understand the dynamics of debt and confidence see the same crisis at two different points in the financial system—already priced in on one side, still waiting patiently on the other! Unless the ECB intervenes, financing conditions will tighten, with potentially unpredictable consequences for banks, lending, growth and overall risk appetite. For gold and silver, higher risk premiums, fiscal dominance, potential central bank intervention, uncertainty over real interest rates and a weaker euro could become key drivers over the medium term. In addition, the round USD 50 level for silver and the USD 4,000 level for gold are coming into focus. Both levels are technically significant and provide strong support. Silver also has a historical component that leads us to expect the precious metals could turn higher around the levels mentioned over the coming weeks through approximately mid-December. We therefore view the current period of weakness not as a warning sign, but as a normal correction within an intact secular bull market and a rare buying opportunity for long-term investors. However, France currently fails to meet precisely this requirement: A significant portion of the spread widening is the result of understandable fiscal and political risks and therefore cannot readily be classified as “unwarranted.” An Allianz research paper sums it up: Only in the event of broader fragmentation in the euro bond market —for example, with French spreads at around 175 basis points, Italian spreads at about 150 basis points, and spreads in Spain and Portugal rising at the same time— would the ECB likely take operational action . The TPI would probably only be considered if the French spread rises above 200 basis points and the Italian spread above 175 basis points Until then, the ECB could initially remain on the sidelines. The market penalty thus acts like an unintended but tangible tightening of monetary policy: More tax revenue goes toward debt service, while fewer funds are available for investment, education and social benefits . At the same time, borrowing becomes more expensive for businesses and households—with adverse consequences for growth, investment activity and purchasing power. Stock markets ignore mounting stress While the eurozone’s fundamentals are increasingly deteriorating and precious metals prices are correcting, equity markets continue to price in relative calm—even though stress is clearly building in the background. Markets are currently telling two contradictory stories. We discussed a similar picture last week for the S&P 500, where bullish and bearish market signals are appearing at the same time. These macroeconomic discrepancies are particularly noteworthy because, over the medium term, one of the two sides is highly likely to be wrong. The key question, therefore, is which market is telling the more fundamentally sound story—and which is merely being driven by momentum, positioning, and short-term capital flows. The silver price provides a textbook example of exactly this: Over the past nine months, the silver market has undergone a sharp and uncompromising correction—without signaling the end of the secular bull market. While the still-ongoing pullback toward USD 50 is an extremely unpleasant stress test for late entrants and a painful lesson in market volatility, anyone who has been active in the precious metals sector long enough knows that these are buying opportunities , as the structural drivers of the bull market remain intact. Correction does not mark the end of the cycle Silver combines monetary demand, industrial use and an extremely small market capitalization. This combination produces both strong upward moves and sharp pullbacks. Meanwhile, the debt crisis, uncertainty over real interest rates and geopolitical fragmentation remain unresolved, while industrial demand for silver, the “critical metal of the future,” is more likely to rise than fall going forward. If the French crisis were to broaden into wider euro fragmentation, the environment for precious metals would change fundamentally. Higher risk premiums, potential ECB intervention, fiscal dominance, and a weaker euro have historically provided favorable conditions for gold and silver . The current correction would then not contradict the crisis, but rather represent its effects being priced in ahead of time. Silver in US dollars – Extremely strong support around USD 50 Silver in US dollars, daily chart as of October 23, 2026. © GOLD.DE With an intraday low of 53.45 so far, silver today fell below its summer low of USD 54.77. Since August 28, the silver price has also essentially moved in only one direction—downward—as interim recoveries have been scarce since the summer high of USD 71.17. However, following a decline of around 25 percent within eight weeks, technical conditions are deeply oversold. The pullback toward USD 50 was to be expected within the decade-long cup-and-handle pattern and is not yet complete . The USD 50 level is crucial, as this is where the 1980 and 2011 highs were located. In the fall of 2025, silver broke above this threshold on a sustained basis for the first time—triggering the subsequent steep rise to USD 121.67. However, the correction underway since January does not automatically invalidate this breakout. So far, it appears to be testing the breakout level in classic fashion. For now, this leaves the daily and weekly charts bearish. Around USD 50, however, the bears are encountering increasingly strong support as well as contrarian buyers. The seasonal pattern also suggests that the final trend reversal should take place by around mid-December—and thus by the Fed’s final interest rate decision of the year. We are therefore not overly concerned. Instead, we now see good buying opportunities again at last in both precious metals and mining stocks, and are therefore consistently using the current period of weakness to make further purchases. Conclusion: Silver – Near its key level The sharp widening of France’s bond spread is once again exposing the fragile political and fiscal foundations of the eurozone. Silver, by contrast, is undergoing a painful but still constructive consolidation following an extreme period of overheating. Those who look only at the daily charts see two weak markets; those who understand the dynamics of debt and confidence see the same crisis at two different points in the financial system—already priced in on one side, still waiting patiently on the other! Unless the ECB intervenes, financing conditions will tighten, with potentially unpredictable consequences for banks, lending, growth and overall risk appetite. For gold and silver, higher risk premiums, fiscal dominance, potential central bank intervention, uncertainty over real interest rates and a weaker euro could become key drivers over the medium term. In addition, the round USD 50 level for silver and the USD 4,000 level for gold are coming into focus. Both levels are technically significant and provide strong support. Silver also has a historical component that leads us to expect the precious metals could turn higher around the levels mentioned over the coming weeks through approximately mid-December. We therefore view the current period of weakness not as a warning sign, but as a normal correction within an intact secular bull market and a rare buying opportunity for long-term investors. news.title: Mozambique approves Moma processing and export rights renewal to 2044[SMM Titanium Flash] Kenmare Resources announced that Mozambique had approved renewal of key processing and export rights under Moma’s Implementation Agreement until 2044. The Council of Ministers adopted its resolution on 13 October and Kenmare received official notification on 29 October. The revised terms raise the royalty on gross revenues from 1% to 3% for 2025–2029, 4% for 2030–2034 and 5% for 2035–2044. The approval provides greater visibility over the operating framework for a major African titanium feedstock exporter, while increasing its royalty burden and investment commitments. Kenmare’s processing subsidiary undertakes to invest at least US$200 million in plant, machinery and infrastructure over the extension period. An agreement addendum still requires signing, followed by administrative procedures involving Mozambique’s Administrative Court. The announcement concerns processing and exports; mining is governed separately, and the renewal does not itself establish additional titanium output.10 hours ago
